learning_outcomes.text: To know the concept of power transmission by means of a fluid.
To evaluate oleo-hydraulic and pneumatic systems establishing the differences between them.
To know the different types of volumetric machines and the selection criteria.
To know the different actuator devices and installation methods.
To know the different systems used to regulate a circuit.
To know ways to dimension the elements of a circuit.
To introduce the concept of closed circuits. To know the steady and unsteady operations of hydrostatic transmissions.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Fundamental principles of power transmission in fluids.
Introduction: Elements of a basic hydraulic circuit.
Introduction: Oleo-hydraulic fluids.
Introduction: Elements of a basic pneumatic circuit.
Introduction: Air compression, conditioning and distribution.
Introduction: Differences between hydraulics and pneumatics.
Introduction: Applications.
Hydraulic pumps: Types of pumps.
Hydraulic pumps: Operation of pumps. Characteristic curves and efficiencies.
Hydraulic pumps: Selection of a pump for an application.
Cylinders: Types of cylinders and constructive elements.
Cylinders: Operation of cylinders.
Cylinders: Selection of a cylinder for an application.
Cylinders: Basic circuits for direct and indirect control of cylinders. Applications.
Motors: Types of motors and constructive elements.
Motors: Operation of motors. Characteristic curves and efficiencies.
Motors: Selection of a motor for an application.
Motors: Basic circuits for direct and indirect control of motors. Applications.
Motors: Hydrostatic transmissions.
Pressure valves: Pressure valves. Constructive elements.
Pressure valves: Operation of pressure valves. Characteristic curves.
Pressure valves: Selection of a pressure valve for an application.
Pressure valves: Circuits with pressure valves. Applications.
Flow valves: Flow valves. Constructive elements.
Flow valves: Operation of flow valves. Characteristic curves.
Flow valves: Selection of a flow valve for an application.
Flow valves: Circuits with flow valves. Applications.
Directional control valves: Directional control valves. Constructive elements.
Directional control valves: Operation of directional control valves. Characteristic curves.
Directional control valves: Selection of a directional control valve for an application.
Directional control valves: Circuits with directional control valves. Applications.
Laboratory Practical Activities - Hydraulics H1: Calibration of the safety valve. Characteristics and operation of a pump and a motor.
Laboratory Practical Activities - Hydraulics H2: Characteristics and operation of a double-acting cylinder. Pressure losses in lines.
Laboratory Practical Activities - Hydraulics H3: Circuits with vertical loads. Regulation of load speed.
Laboratory Practical Activities - Hydraulics H4: Counterbalance valves. Circuits for regulating load speed.
Laboratory Practical Activities - Hydraulics H5: Operation of circuits with multiple actuators.
Laboratory Practical Activities - Pneumatics N1: Direct control of single-acting and double-acting cylinders.
Laboratory Practical Activities - Pneumatics N2: Indirect control of single-acting and double-acting cylinders. Speed regulation.
Laboratory Practical Activities - Pneumatics N3: Logic valves in pneumatics.
Laboratory Practical Activities - Pneumatics N4: Circuits with multiple actuators. Signal timing.
Laboratory Practical Activities - Pneumatics N5: Circuits with rodless cylinder and vacuum ejectors.
assessment_rules: The final grade (fi) is calculated using different formulas for ordinary, extraordinary, and global evaluation calls, each summing weighted scores from a partial exam (hs), final exam (hi), laboratory practices (so), a project (su), or an exam of laboratory practices (hso). A minimum score of 4 out of 10 is generally required in the final exam (hi) and/or the lab practices exam (hso) for the weighted sum (f) to apply; otherwise, the final grade is capped at 4. Partial exams and laboratory practices are not recoverable, meaning they cannot be retaken in the extraordinary call, while the final exam and project are recoverable. In multiple-choice tests, wrong answers deduct one-third of the correct answer's value.
